summary: In this excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 6, part 170), Russell recalls that Arthur has said his earlier help was a matter of convenience, and Arthur reports that Sonya Halliday secured a deal with the Feds, under which Agent Jones agreed to make the matter go away. Arthur then tells Russell that Dr. Martinez, who is seriously ill, may have been hallucinating, which raises the possibility that the proof she wrote was nonsense. Russell is shaken, feels that nothing is real, and is offered a chance to visit Martinez before he refuses to see the point.
one_line: Russell learns from Arthur that Halliday secured a deal with the Feds and that Martinez, gravely ill, may have imagined the proof she wrote.
key_facts: Arthur tells Russell that the arrangement with the Feds was Sonya's doing, since she kept her cool and held her ground.
Arthur says Sonya told the Feds they had to leave Russell be, and Agent Jones agreed to make it all go away.
Russell wonders whether Halliday knows what he did in going after her friend, and whether she defended him out of forgiveness or to keep him working with her.
Russell thinks Halliday does not know he is damaged, forever now.
When Russell asks whether Martinez will recover, Martinez answers that they are not hopeful.
Martinez tells Russell that one symptom of her illness is hallucinations, and that she might have been thinking things that are not real.
Arthur suggests Martinez may have burned her own scribbles in a fit of madness and then stolen her friend's legitimate work because her illness imagined demons.
Russell says the proof might have been nothing but nonsense, and he feels that nothing is real.
Russell asks Martinez's whereabouts: "You don't think she ever had the proof," he murmurs, and Arthur answers, "Don't know. Likely we'll never know."
Arthur says that Dr. Martinez can be visited because the staff are letting them see her.
Russell asks what the point of a visit would be, and says he did not know Martinez that well.
Russell says that Martinez had destroyed him.
